- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts rise sharply, cap the upward slope to avoid overshoot after recent spikes.  
- If official supply net is negative and bullish sentiment is low, model should not overcorrect upward — expect mean reversion toward lower range.  
- After a spike in price (e.g., >75), model should not assume continuation — reduce forecast slope for next 3–5 days to allow for volatility decay.  
- When sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, reduce forecast magnitude by 5–10% to avoid false bullish bias.  
- If official event count is high and supply net is negative, model should not overestimate price rise — expect downward pressure in 3–7 day horizon.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome deviates >10% from 15-day moving average, adjust forecast to align with recent mean reversion trend.  
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model should not assume linear trend — use weighted average of recent sentiment to adjust slope.
